findings.summary: the settlement requires a ledger row with a promoted_revision, which the node's goal does not name, so a run whose delivery the primary carries but which has no ledger row still replays its gate; the narrowing is deliberate and pinned by the no-row test, but it leaves the reported re-request case unsettled whenever no promotion ever wrote a row

rows[0]["gate"] == "passed" compares the ledger value against the literal the fixture itself wrote at line 219 rather than an independent source, so it only catches a rewrite that changes the value; the zero-replay assertion at line 262 carries the guard

the promotion_request_for_a_landed_delivery fixture repeats the worktree, pointer and monkeypatch setup of the existing settled_delivery fixture at line 59 in the same file instead of extending it, so the two setups can drift apart

the base-revision negative control the done_when names (the first added case failing on a counted gate replay) is recorded only in the run's stream.jsonl; the negative_control_log the manifest files is the mutation of the third case, so the named control has no log a later reader can open

item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit 823a9536 against its base; it adds _carried_delivery_settlement and SETTLEABLE_KINDS, adds settle_a_carried_delivery and refactors _land_deliveries onto it, and adds four test cases, with no other file changed.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's done_when names tests/test_a_landed_head_is_not_landed_again.py; the manifest's scoped-gate log records 66 passed at 823a9536a8, and the three named cases plus a no-ledger-row case are present in the added 147 lines.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to settle a promotion request whose head and changed paths are already on the primary branch; reckon/crew/promotion_requests.py:629 settles such a request before executing it, but only when a ledger row with a promoted_revision is already written, so a carried run with no row still replays.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, the commit 823a9536a8, the gate command, both suite arms (62 then 66 passed, exit 0) and a negative-control log at the declared path.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's five declared paths; the delivered diff touches only reckon/crew/promotion_requests.py, reckon/crew/queue_landing.py and tests/test_a_landed_head_is_not_landed_again.py, all inside them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_landed_head_is_not_landed_again.py:262 counts gate replays through a monkeypatched promotion step, so removing the settlement makes the assertion red exactly as the recorded base-revision run shows.
justifications.evidence: the gate and both suite arms are recorded green at 823a9536a8 (66 passed) and 65c0479b14 (62 passed) with zero added failures, and the base-revision red run of the first added case survives only in the observed run's stream.jsonl, not as a log.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:117 names its stage constants CARRIED_SETTLED/CARRIED_HELD and documents the helper the way the module's other stage vocabulary is documented.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion_requests.py:653 returns no settlement when the run has no ledger row, so a carried delivery without a row still takes the ordinary path and replays its gate.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:124 wraps pending_landing._release_integrated_pointer and reuses _primary_carries_the_delivery, but the new fixture at tests/test_a_landed_head_is_not_landed_again.py:192 repeats the setup of the existing settled_delivery fixture at line 59.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the commit is one of the three declared source/test paths; the declared evidence fragment and figure directory under docs/ are untouched.
